payload.message:
JIRA sprint task allocation. Each agent chooses at most one micro-task (or skips). Maximize tasks completed, prefer higher-priority tasks, then minimize total cost. Avoid duplicate task selections and infeasible assignments.

NOTE: If environment.assignment_filling=true and an agent fails to assign a variable, the environment will fill any remaining unassigned variables with a uniform-random allowed assignment when producing final results.

This blackboard is a private communication channel.
Participants: Arletha, Junko, Myrle, Shari

payload.content:
Hi all — Arletha here. Availability 5.0h, top skill testing:0.92. My costs strongly favor the ISSUE-0002 testing track. Cheapest feasible for me is ISSUE-0002::review (cost 3.93, medium priority). I plan to claim ISSUE-0002::review.

Please reply with your intended task so we avoid duplicates:
- Junko, Myrle, Shari: which tasks are cheapest for you? Prefer to cover the medium-priority ISSUE-0002 tasks (implement/review/test) since they carry more priority weight, then fill ISSUE-0001 low-priority tasks.

I'll take ISSUE-0002::review unless someone has a much stronger claim to it. Suggest we each announce one distinct task.

Hi all — Shari here. Availability 7.0h, top skills backend:0.94, testing:0.83.

My costs (low→high):
- ISSUE-0001::triage 1.16 (low)
- ISSUE-0001::review 1.45 (low)
- ISSUE-0001::docs 1.45 (low)
- ISSUE-0001::test 2.03 (low)
- ISSUE-0001::implement 2.89 (low)
- ISSUE-0002::review 4.30 (medium)
- ISSUE-0002::test 6.02 (medium)
- ISSUE-0002::implement 9.59 (medium, and effort 8.0h > my 7.0h so effectively infeasible for me)

I'm clearly cheapest on the backend (ISSUE-0001) track, so the efficient split is for me to cover a 0001 task while the testing specialists cover ISSUE-0002.

However, I can also handle ISSUE-0002::test (medium) if needed — avail 7.0 ≥ effort 5.6.

Questions:
- Junko / Myrle: what are your availabilities and cheapest tasks? Specifically, can either of you do ISSUE-0002::implement (effort 8.0, needs ≥8h)?
- Arletha: noted, you take ISSUE-0002::review.

My tentative intent: take a low-priority ISSUE-0001 backend task (cheapest = triage 1.16) UNLESS a medium 0002 task would otherwise go uncovered — in which case I'll take ISSUE-0002::test to secure the extra priority weight.

Goal: 3 medium (0002) + 1 low (0001) claimed if implement is feasible for someone; otherwise 2 medium + 2 low. Please state one distinct task each so we avoid duplicates.

Arletha here — confirming my plan. Availability 5.0h, so ISSUE-0002::test (effort 5.6) and ISSUE-0002::implement (effort 8.0) are INFEASIBLE for me. My only medium-priority feasible task is ISSUE-0002::review (effort 4.0, cost 3.93), and it's also my cheapest overall. So I am claiming ISSUE-0002::review.

Efficient split I propose:
- Arletha -> ISSUE-0002::review (medium) ✅
- Shari -> a low ISSUE-0001 task (your cheapest is triage 1.16); you're the backend specialist, leave 0002 to testing folks.
- Junko / Myrle -> please confirm availability. We still need coverage of ISSUE-0002::test (effort 5.6) and ISSUE-0002::implement (effort 8.0, requires >=8h availability). If neither of you has >=8h, implement is likely infeasible for everyone and we should cover the remaining medium (test) plus fill 0001 tasks.

Please each state ONE distinct task so we avoid duplicate claims. (phase=planning, iter=1)

Shari here — replying to Arletha's split (iter=1, planning).

Agreed: Arletha keeps ISSUE-0002::review (medium). No objection.

My decision rule (so we don't dither):
- DEFAULT (if the two medium 0002 tasks are covered by others): I take ISSUE-0001::triage (low, my cheapest at cost 1.16, effort 1.2h ≪ my 7.0h). This maximizes tasks done + low cost.
- FALLBACK (if ISSUE-0002::test would otherwise go uncovered): I take ISSUE-0002::test (medium, effort 5.6h ≤ my 7.0h, cost 6.02) to secure the extra priority weight, and someone else takes a 0001 task.
- I CANNOT do ISSUE-0002::implement: effort 8.0h > my 7.0h availability → infeasible for me.

Junko / Myrle — you still haven't stated your availability or costs. Two things we need from you:
1) Does EITHER of you have availability ≥ 8.0h? That's the only way ISSUE-0002::implement (medium) is feasible at all. If no one has ≥8h, implement is out and we should target 2 medium + 2 low.
2) Who takes ISSUE-0002::test (needs ≥5.6h)? If one of you takes it, I'll take 0001::triage.

Target outcome:
- If someone ≥8h: implement + review + test (3 medium) + my 0001 (1 low) = 4 tasks.
- Else: review + test (2 medium) + two 0001 tasks (2 low) = 4 tasks.

Please each reply with ONE distinct task. I'll finalize my pick in execution based on your answers.

Myrle here. Availability 10.0h, top skills testing:0.71, backend:0.69.

Key fact: I am the ONLY agent with >=8.0h availability, so ISSUE-0002::implement (effort 8.0, medium) is feasible ONLY for me. To maximize tasks done + priority, I will claim ISSUE-0002::implement.

My costs (low->high): 0001::triage 1.52, 0001::review 1.90, 0001::docs 1.90, 0001::test 2.65, 0001::implement 3.79, 0002::review 4.97, 0002::test 6.95, 0002::implement 9.93.

Proposed efficient split (4 agents, 4 tasks = 3 medium + 1 low):
- Myrle -> ISSUE-0002::implement (medium) [only feasible for me]
- Arletha -> ISSUE-0002::review (medium) [your cheapest]
- Shari -> ISSUE-0002::test (medium, effort 5.6 <= 7.0h) OR ISSUE-0001::triage (low, your cheapest 1.16)
- Junko -> whichever of {0002::test, 0001::triage} Shari doesn't take

This gives 3 medium + 1 low with no duplicates and no infeasibility. Junko: please state your availability + cheapest task so we finalize. Shari: if Junko can take 0002::test, please take 0001::triage; otherwise you take 0002::test. (phase=planning, iter=1)

Arletha here — final confirmation for planning (iter=1).

My pick is settled: ISSUE-0002::review (medium, effort 4.0 ≤ 5.0h, cost 3.93 — my cheapest feasible and my only feasible medium task). ISSUE-0002::test (5.6h) and ::implement (8.0h) are both INFEASIBLE for me given 5.0h availability.

Endorsing Myrle's split:
- Myrle -> ISSUE-0002::implement (only agent with ≥8h) ✅
- Arletha -> ISSUE-0002::review ✅
- Shari -> ISSUE-0002::test (medium) if Junko can't, else ISSUE-0001::triage (low)
- Junko -> the remaining {0002::test, 0001::triage}

Junko: please state ONE task. If you can take ISSUE-0002::test (needs ≥5.6h), Shari takes 0001::triage → 3 medium + 1 low. If not, Shari takes 0002::test and you take a 0001 low task → 2 medium + 2 low.

No duplicates, no infeasibility. I'll commit ISSUE-0002::review in execution.

Junko here. Availability 9.0h, top skill backend:0.74.

My costs: 0001::triage=1.44, 0001::review=1.80, 0001::docs=1.80, 0001::test=2.51, 0001::implement=3.59, but 0002 tasks are prohibitively expensive for me (0002::review=40, 0002::test=56, 0002::implement=80). So I am NOT a good fit for any 0002 task even though I have the hours.

My claim: ISSUE-0001::triage (low, cost 1.44, effort 1.2h).

This fits the efficient split:
- Myrle -> ISSUE-0002::implement (medium, only agent with >=8h)
- Arletha -> ISSUE-0002::review (medium)
- Shari -> ISSUE-0002::test (medium, 5.6h <= 7.0h)
- Junko -> ISSUE-0001::triage (low)

Result: 3 medium + 1 low = 4 tasks (max possible with 4 agents), no duplicates, no infeasibility, minimal total cost. Shari: please take 0002::test (not triage) since it's far cheaper for you than for me. Committing ISSUE-0001::triage in execution.

EXECUTION: Junko committing ISSUE-0001::triage (low priority, cost 1.44, effort 1.2h <= 9.0h availability). Final allocation: Myrle=0002::implement, Arletha=0002::review, Shari=0002::test, Junko=0001::triage. 4 tasks, 3 medium + 1 low, no duplicates, no infeasibility.

Arletha here — locking in my planning choice. I claim ISSUE-0002::review (medium, effort 4.0 ≤ my 5.0h, cost 3.93 — my cheapest feasible task and my ONLY feasible medium task; 0002::test at 5.6h and 0002::implement at 8.0h are infeasible for me).

Final allocation (no duplicates, no infeasibility):
- Myrle -> ISSUE-0002::implement (medium; only agent with ≥8h)
- Arletha -> ISSUE-0002::review (medium)
- Shari -> ISSUE-0002::test (medium; effort 5.6h ≤ 7.0h)
- Junko -> ISSUE-0001::triage (low)

= 4 tasks, 3 medium + 1 low, minimal total cost. Shari: please take 0002::test as agreed (it's far cheaper for you than for Junko). I'll commit ISSUE-0002::review in execution. (phase=planning, iter=1)

Shari here — confirming the final split (iter=1, planning).

I accept my role: I will claim ISSUE-0002::test (medium, effort 5.6h ≤ my 7.0h availability, my cost 6.02). This is feasible for me and far cheaper than for Junko (who quoted ~56). Taking it secures the third medium task — better for the joint score than me taking a low 0001 task.

Final allocation (no duplicates, no infeasibility):
- Myrle -> ISSUE-0002::implement (medium; only agent with ≥8h)
- Arletha -> ISSUE-0002::review (medium)
- Shari -> ISSUE-0002::test (medium)
- Junko -> ISSUE-0001::triage (low)

= 4 tasks, 3 medium + 1 low, minimal total cost. No objections to Arletha/Myrle/Junko's stated claims. I'll commit ISSUE-0002::test in execution. (phase=planning, iter=1)

Junko — FINAL (planning, iter=1). I confirm my single claim: ISSUE-0001::triage (low, effort 1.2h ≤ 9.0h, cost 1.44 — my cheapest feasible task; all 0002 tasks are prohibitively expensive for me: 40/56/80).

Locked allocation (4 tasks, 3 medium + 1 low, no duplicates, no infeasibility, minimal cost):
- Myrle -> ISSUE-0002::implement (medium; only agent with ≥8h)
- Arletha -> ISSUE-0002::review (medium)
- Shari -> ISSUE-0002::test (medium)
- Junko -> ISSUE-0001::triage (low)

This maximizes tasks done (4 = max with 4 agents) and priority (3 medium + 1 low = 1.75) at the lowest total cost. Everyone please commit your stated task so no slot is left to random filling. No objections.
